title: L40S preset + memory/KV-cache guardrails for hardware tuning profiles pack
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Goal
Ship an L40S-tuned runtime profile focused on stability under memory pressure (KV cache sizing + fragmentation guardrails) and “safe batching” defaults that avoid OOMs and avoid p95 latency spikes for long-context + moderate concurrency workloads.

Context
During first-pass workload-matrix runs on L40S runners we saw intermittent CUDA OOMs and non-linear p95 latency spikes when:
- prompt length mix includes long prefill buckets (8k–16k) alongside short requests,
- concurrency > ~8 (varies by model + quantization), and
- continuous batching aggressively admits work without accounting for KV cache growth + fragmentation.

This ticket delivers a preset that is safe-by-default for Hosted/Dedicated L40S pools, plus guardrails that keep Private deployments supportable (clear headroom, explicit rejection/backpressure behavior instead of “best effort until OOM”).

Scope
In-scope
- L40S profile defaults for:
  - KV cache budget + watermark behavior
  - max in-flight tokens / max queued tokens
  - prefill vs decode fairness parameters tuned to avoid tail blow-ups
  - conservative continuous batching knobs for memory-bounded GPUs
- Memory guardrails:
  - admission control using KV-cache growth estimates (prefill and decode)
  - explicit headroom reserved for weights/activations + fragmentation
  - “fail closed” behavior: reject/429 (or shed) before OOM; never kernel-crash the worker
- Regression checks for:
  - OOM rate (hard fail) and near-OOM (allocator retries / emergency eviction)
  - p95/p99 latency spikes correlated with batch growth or KV pressure

Out of scope
- Writing new kernels or allocator rewrites
- Customer-specific per-model hand tuning beyond the profile schema

Proposed L40S profile behavior (v1)
1) KV cache budgeting
- Set a hard KV cache budget (bytes) derived from detected GPU memory and runtime reserved memory.
- Enforce a watermark-based behavior:
  - At “soft” watermark: stop admitting new long-prefill requests; prefer draining.
  - At “hard” watermark: reject requests that would exceed budget, emit a structured log + metric.
- Prefer deterministic budgeting over opportunistic growth (L40S fragmentation sensitivity is higher than H100).

2) Safe batching defaults
- Cap max_batch_total_tokens to prevent “batch ballooning” under mixed prompt distributions.
- Lower queue depth for long-prefill buckets; enforce backpressure earlier.
- Keep decode concurrency moderate; avoid decode starvation that inflates end-to-end latency.

3) Guardrail semantics
- If request cannot be admitted within constraints, return a clear overload response (rate-limit style) with retry-after, rather than letting the worker OOM.
- Emit high-cardinality-free metrics that oncall can segment by:
  - profile name/version
  - rejection reason: kv_budget, queue_limit, batch_token_cap

Implementation notes (targets)
- Profile name: l40s/balanced/v1 (exact naming per schema doc)
- Knobs to set in profile (final list to match schema):
  - kv_cache.budget_bytes / budget_fraction
  - kv_cache.soft_watermark_fraction, kv_cache.hard_watermark_fraction
  - scheduler.max_batch_total_tokens
  - scheduler.max_prefill_tokens_per_batch
  - scheduler.max_inflight_requests
  - scheduler.queue_limit_requests / queue_limit_tokens
  - scheduler.prefill_decode_fairness_mode (conservative)
  - scheduler.backpressure_mode (admission-control enabled)

Acceptance criteria
Functional
- L40S profile can be selected via runtime profile loader and surfaced in metrics/debug endpoint (handled in ENG-4823/ENG-22027 but validate end-to-end here).
- Runtime rejects gracefully when KV cache budget would be exceeded (no worker crash, no CUDA OOM).

Performance / stability
- Workload-matrix (L40S) “long-context mix” scenarios complete with:
  - 0 CUDA OOM events
  - OOM-prevented rejections allowed, but must be bounded and visible (metric + log)
- p95 latency regression vs baseline (no profile) in the “standard mix” scenarios:
  - <= +5% p95 end-to-end, averaged across 3 runs
  - no single scenario > +10% p95 without a documented trade-off + explicit workload envelope
- Throughput impact:
  - tokens/sec can regress up to 5% in worst-case long-context scenarios if it materially improves stability; must be documented in expected behavior doc (ENG-4829)

Regression checks to add/update
- Perf suite:
  - Add/enable a long-context, mixed prompt distribution case on L40S runners.
  - Pin concurrency levels (e.g., 4/8/12) to catch admission-control edges.
- Perf canary:
  - Gate on OOM count == 0
  - Gate on p95 and p99 within agreed bands for L40S pools
  - Alert on sudden increases in kv_budget_rejections (rate + absolute)

Rollout plan (owned by Infra/SRE but this ticket must be “rollout-ready”)
- Start in one L40S canary pool (us-east) with profile enabled.
- Ramp from 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 48 hours if gates are green.
- Rollback criteria: any CUDA OOM > 0 OR sustained p95 +15% for 30m OR error rate +0.5% absolute.

comments: 2025-11-19 — Samir Qureshi: Reproduced OOM on L40S with 16k prefill bucket + concurrency 12 (mixed short + long). Fragmentation shows up after ~20–30 min steady load; OOM happens even with reported free mem > 2GB. Plan: introduce explicit KV budget + hard admission control, keep 10–12% headroom to account for allocator fragmentation and transient activation spikes.

2025-11-20 — Omar El-Sayed: KV-cache growth estimate needs to include decode continuation tokens (streaming). Suggest budgeting by (max_new_tokens * concurrent_streams) in addition to prefill. Also need a clear rejection reason metric so Support can distinguish overload vs regression.

2025-11-22 — Lena Fischer: For L40S we should keep max_batch_total_tokens conservative; batching wins are smaller when memory is the limiting factor. Recommend we bias toward tail stability even if tokens/sec is slightly lower than baseline in long-context cases.

2025-11-25 — Rina Kobayashi: Added draft workload matrix case: long-prefill (8k–16k) + tool-like short prompts mixed 70/30; concurrency 8 and 12. This is the one currently flaking due to OOM. Will wire into perf runner once guardrails land.

2025-11-29 — Samir Qureshi: Implemented KV budget fraction default for L40S profile and hard watermark rejection. Early results: 0 OOMs across 6 runs; we see ~0.8–1.6% kv_budget_rejections at concurrency 12. p95 improves vs baseline (baseline had long tail due to allocator thrash).

2025-12-02 — Aisha Bello (SRE): Please ensure logs/metrics do not include request IDs/prompt lengths as labels. We only want low-cardinality reason codes + profile version. Also add a dashboard panel for kv_budget_rejections correlated with p95 so oncall can quickly decide rollback vs expected behavior.

2025-12-04 — Samir Qureshi: PR up with guardrails + KV budgeting defaults + rollback toggle. Added runtime log line summarizing computed KV budget and reserved headroom at startup. Included a config knob to disable admission control for emergency comparisons (default stays enabled for L40S profile).

2025-12-06 — Ethan Park: Marking Done. PR-22015 merged. Follow-ups: (1) ensure perf-canary thresholds updated (ENG-4828), (2) document expected behavior for L40S (ENG-4829), (3) confirm Helm values exposure for Private overrides (ENG-4823 / helm PR-612).
